closes: Whether the optimizer's declared path grammar is an injective, total addressing function over emitter-controlled gate trees (measured live, both resolver sites).
Whether a hard-constraint verdict can be changed by keys the envelope emitter adds without touching the constrained gate.
Whether the two shipped resolvers of the one declared grammar agree on their domain.
does_not_close: Operators other than '==' at the constraint site (covered by optimizer-authorization-numeric-comparison-conformance-v1).
The `section` field's own name space (only 'gates' is exercised at the constraint site, since the contract fixes it).

Whether any shipped KPI profile currently declares a path that triggers these behaviours -- shipped profiles use single-segment paths, so the exposure measured here is contract-level, not an observed production miscount.
Any scientific claim about coatings; this is an infrastructure authorization-surface audit.

H0a_injectivity.detail: empty path segments are discarded, so the separator padding of a path text is semantically inert: many distinct declared texts bind the same node

H0b_addressability.detail: a node is reachable under the shipped grammar iff every step on its root path is a non-empty, dot-free object member name whose joined text survives the trimming declaration guard; empty keys, whitespace-only keys, keys containing '.', array elements and the gates root itself are unreachable by construction

H0c_non_shadowing.detail: a flat gate key containing '.' is unreachable, and the text that names it is captured by a nested object the emitter may add unilaterally; the same declared constraint therefore changes verdict as a function of emitter-controlled keys (CWE-706)

verdict_flip.reason_without: optimizer constraint path is absent or unknown

cross_site_grammar_divergence.detail: the constraint site requires at least one segment and rejects a whitespace-only declaration, while the display site folds from the section value and returns the whole gates object for a segmentless path: two resolvers of one declared grammar do not agree on their domain

mediation_completeness.detail: display-side path resolution is performed outside the reference monitor: gate values of envelopes the monitor refuses are still resolved and surfaced (Saltzer-Schroeder complete mediation)
mediation_completeness.reading_note: site_b_feasible is produced under a display-only profile that declares NO hard constraints, so it reports a constraint-free authorization and must not be read as an endorsement of the mutated envelope. M1-M6 mutate envelope ADMISSION fields, which the monitor checks for every envelope, so authorization errors and feasible is false. M7 mutates status, which the monitor only checks for a module some declared constraint names: with no constraint declared, a FAILED envelope is surfaced AND reported feasible. The non-SCORED count remains visible separately in RankedCandidate.failed_modules, recorded per row as site_b_failed_modules.

hypothesis.H0a_injectivity: distinct accepted path texts address distinct gate nodes
hypothesis.H0b_addressability: every node of a legal RFC 8259 gates tree is addressable by some path text
hypothesis.H0c_non_shadowing: the node a path text binds does not depend on keys the envelope emitter may add

method_lineage: Black-box node identification by discriminating equality probes over a corpus whose leaves are pairwise distinct; two-site live differential; characterisation theorem for the reachable node set checked against the live measurement.
non_circularity: Site A resolution is identified black-box: the probe never reads the runtime resolver, it sweeps '==' over every distinct node value in the corpus and infers the bound node from which probe the live authorization accepts. Site B returns its resolved value verbatim. The Python oracle is written from the declared grammar and from RFC 6901/RFC 8259, and imports no runtime code.
proposed_hardeners: Replace the ad-hoc `section`+dotted-`path` pair in OptimizerConstraintRequestV1 / DisplayKpi with a single RFC 6901 JSON Pointer field, and reject any pointer that does not begin with '/' -- this makes the addressing function total and injective and removes the separator-padding orbit entirely.

Until the contract changes, reject at declaration time any path text that is not equal to '.'.join(segments(text)) -- i.e. refuse leading, trailing and doubled separators rather than silently normalising them away.

Reject at admission time any envelope whose `gates` tree contains a member name that is empty or contains '.', since such a gate is unconstrainable and its name is capturable by an emitter-added nested object.
Route display-KPI resolution through the same admission check as the constraint site, so no gate value of a refused envelope is resolved or surfaced (complete mediation).
Unify the two resolvers into one function so that the domain of the constraint site and the display site cannot drift apart.
purpose: Audit the constraint/display path-addressing grammar of the optimizer reference monitor as an addressing function over the emitter-controlled `gates` tree: is it injective, is it complete, and is the node a declared path binds independent of keys the envelope emitter may add? Compare against RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, the published standard for addressing JSON nodes.

rfc6901_repair.why_total: RFC 6901 Sec. 3 escapes '~' and '/' and treats every other character literally, so '.' and the empty member name are spellable; Sec. 4 gives array elements decimal index tokens; the empty pointer denotes the root. The token sequence is in bijection with the node's root path, so the addressing function is total and injective.
